clue.text: Reduced watch for petty criminal maybe

parts.note: something reduced has been made small
a watch is a timer, a device that keeps time

explanation.surface: A cut-price wristwatch is just the thing for a minor crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-time crook is a minor offender, so a petty thief is one example of such a person.

clue.text: Religious group caught in position

indicators.note: in says the letter for caught is placed inside the word for position

parts.note: a set can mean a fixed position or posture
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Members of a religious group are trapped in an awkward spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a breakaway body of believers, a religious faction.

clue.text: A very quiet place for filming comedies is attracting interest

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
Ealing Studios in west London made the famous Ealing comedies

explanation.surface: A hushed studio where comedies are shot proves alluring to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a London district whose film studios made the celebrated post-war Ealing comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appealing draws people towards it, the same as attracting their interest.

clue.text: Grub from river running through soft rock

indicators.note: running through says the river's letter flows into the middle of the rock word

parts.note: lava is molten rock, soft until it cools

explanation.surface: Food found where a stream cuts through crumbly stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food or digging, but here it is the insect young.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the larval stage of an insect, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Encourage ideas initially on northern part of church

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so this piece comes first
initially means only the opening letter of ideas is taken

parts.note: a spire is the tall pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Fresh thoughts about the church's north side give heart to the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire someone is to fill them with enthusiasm, which is to encourage them.

clue.text: Personal journey in which content of language got riper

indicators.note: content of says the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone's private voyage during which their speech grew ever more ripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal journey' is a playful definition: a self-indulgent venture is a trip for the ego.
explanation.definitionFit: A vanity-driven project is jokingly described as a journey made for one's own self-image.

clue.text: Bundle sporting mates abroad, sending the last one West

indicators.note: in an across clue west is the left, so the final letter is moved to the front

parts.note: WAGs, wives and girlfriends of footballers, became famous travelling to tournaments abroad

explanation.surface: Footballers' partners overseas lug a parcel about, packing off the last of them home.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs is British tabloid slang for the wives and girlfriends of star footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: A swag is a bundle of belongings carried by a traveller in Australian usage, or a thief's loot.

clue.text: Greater suffering encompasses the outskirts of Rheims

indicators.note: encompasses says the word for suffering wraps around the other letters

parts.note: woe is grief or suffering

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Even more pain surrounds the suburbs of the French city of Rheims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greater suffering' reads as one phrase, but 'Greater' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse means more severe, as when a bad situation becomes greater in its badness.

clue.text: Woman marrying for money — or JCB?

definitions.meaning: a woman who courts a rich partner for their wealth
JCB is a British maker of excavators, often finished in yellow, so a golden digging machine

explanation.surface: A fortune-hunting bride is likened to a mechanical excavator.
explanation.walkthrough: JCB is the British brand so common it names any mechanical digger; its machines are yellow, so the question mark plays on a gold-coloured one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names someone who forms relationships purely to get at the partner's riches.

clue.text: Speaking sharply, answer for the first one in cutting

indicators.note: for the first one in says the leading letter I in the next word is swapped out for the new letter

parts.note: snipping means cutting with scissors

explanation.surface: Barking a reply while trimming away, the answer replacing the first thing being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is I, the Roman numeral; the first of the two I's in SNIPPING becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Snapping at someone means retorting irritably, which is speaking sharply.

clue.text: Primate caught in credit scam

indicators.note: caught in says the animal word is trapped inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey is found mixed up in a fraudulent lending racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a mischievous or illegal escapade, so a scam is one example.

clue.text: Villain's cold — nurse getting worried

definitions.note: Villain's stands for villain is, with the 's a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: worried here means shaken or tumbled about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The bad guy has a chill, and the nurse is becoming anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold' looks like the abbreviation C, but the whole word is used: COLD plus NURSE is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rogue, a synonym for a villain.

clue.text: Devil-may-care potholer entertaining tabloid regularly

indicators.note: entertaining means holding within, so the potholer word houses the other letters

parts.note: a potholer explores caves, so is a caver

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of tabloid is taken

explanation.surface: A reckless cave explorer plays host to a gossip newspaper now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand and careless, the same as devil-may-care.

clue.text: Ask for quiet conduct

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
to conduct someone is to lead them

explanation.surface: Request hushed behaviour from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead for something is to beg or ask for it earnestly.

clue.text: Time taken by a measuring of depth is amazing

indicators.note: taken by says the time letter is absorbed inside the following phrase

parts.note: a sounding measures the depth of water

explanation.surface: How long it takes to plumb the sea is quite remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounding and amazing are synonyms, both meaning astonishing.

clue.text: Led off following Cornish home fraud

indicators.note: following places the shuffled letters after the earlier pieces

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the South West of England, abbreviated SW
in means at home

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man led away after a Cornish house scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cornish' gives SW because Cornwall is in England's South West; 'off' scrambles the letters of Led, and 'following' sets them last.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle is a deceitful scheme to cheat someone, a fraud.

clue.text: Contribution from party people

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Gift collected from a political party's members.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift of money given to a cause, a contribution.

clue.text: Union rep finishes broadcasting

indicators.note: finishes means the closing letter of rep is used

parts.note: airing a programme means broadcasting it

explanation.surface: A union representative ends up on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union rep' reads as a trade unionist, but 'Union' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pairing is a joining of two things together, a union.

clue.text: Not moving prisoner, accommodating a new unit

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the prisoner word holds the rest

parts.note: an inmate is a prisoner
I, the Roman numeral one, represents a unit

explanation.surface: A stationary convict takes in a newly arrived unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanimate means lifeless and motionless, not moving.

clue.text: Naturally produced skin, for example, is chilled initially

parts.note: skin is the body's largest organ

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of is and chilled are taken

explanation.surface: Natural skincare products are kept cool from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown naturally without artificial chemicals.

clue.text: Beacon designed to cover western plant

indicators.note: to cover says the rearranged letters wrap around the western letter
designed means arranged anew, so the letters of beacon are reordered

explanation.surface: A signal light made to shelter a plant in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns BEACON into COBANE, and 'to cover' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowbane is a poisonous plant, water hemlock, toxic to cattle.

clue.text: Germany perversely agreed to devalue

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: perversely means contrarily, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Germany has unexpectedly consented to reduce its currency's value.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade something is to lower its worth or standing, to devalue it.

clue.text: Cattle workers formed by origin of Dorking Wanderers

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of Dorking

parts.note: rovers are wanderers

explanation.surface: Farmhands are produced by the start of a football club from Dorking.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorking is a town in Surrey; the surface suggests a football club, as many British teams are called Wanderers or Rovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Drovers drive herds of cattle or sheep to market, so they are livestock workers.

clue.text: Dark and terribly thin, but good at heart

indicators.note: at heart puts the letter in the middle of the shuffled letters
terribly means badly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Gloomy and dreadfully skinny, yet kind deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns THIN into NIHT, and 'at heart' puts G in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark part of the day, and dark is used as a noun for it.

clue.text: Yielded to pressure and left hammer

parts.note: a thing that gave under pressure yielded to it

explanation.surface: Buckled under strain and walked out, leaving a hammer behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavel is the small mallet a judge or auctioneer uses, a type of hammer.

clue.text: Novel question?

parts.note: the key question asked by a detective story, about who committed the crime, also names that kind of book

explanation.definitionFit: A detective mystery novel takes its name from the question it poses about the culprit.

clue.text: Vacates pub, returning distressed

annotationWithheld.why: Vacates pub, returning distressed: the only parse is TESPU hidden across 'Vacates pub' and reversed by 'returning', but no clue word signals the hiding, so 'returning' would do two jobs

clue.text: Acting for the monarchy creates some resistance

definitions.meaning: On Her Majesty's Service, printed on official British government mail

explanation.surface: Royal servants generate a degree of opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: OHMS abbreviates On Her (His) Majesty's Service, printed on British official envelopes; 'creates' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation marks official royal business, and the plural unit measures electrical resistance.

clue.text: Popular musical instrument, note, cannot be touched

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a viola is a stringed instrument
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fashionable stringed instrument note is untouchable.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means free from harm or violation, kept untouched.

clue.text: Demolish sheep's head with potato

indicators.note: head means the first letter of sheep's

parts.note: mash is mashed potato

explanation.surface: A sheep's head served with mashed potatoes, eaten hungrily.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash something is to break it to pieces, to demolish it.

clue.text: Delay retiring before a festive occasion

indicators.note: before places the reversed word ahead of the a
retiring means going back, so the word for delay is read backwards

parts.note: a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: A postponement turns up before a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive celebration or special social event.

clue.text: People putting lignite in rings may be experienced travellers

definitions.meaning: jet is a form of lignite used in jewellery
wealthy people who travel widely by air

explanation.surface: Jewellers mounting jet in rings may be well-travelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are fashionable rich people who fly around the world for pleasure.
